overview: The School Committee received updates on school operations, COVID-19 health protocols, and the proposed FY22 budget while hearing year-end highlights from elementary principals. Key decisions included resuming in-person meetings at City Hall starting in June and extending the deadline for the Columbus Elementary School renaming advisory committee.

items.title: Executive Session and Financial Approvals
items.summary: The committee convened in executive session for collective bargaining strategy before approving bills, payroll, and minutes from several May budget hearings.

items.title: Curriculum Subcommittee Report
items.summary: Member Van der Kloot reported on health and physical education curriculum updates, including alignment with national standards and staffing needs for adaptive physical education.

items.title: Rules, Policy, and Equity Subcommittee Report
items.summary: The committee discussed proposed updates to public participation policies and new meeting agenda formats, referring the draft policies back to subcommittee for further review.

items.title: Approval of Harassment Policy
items.summary: Approved an updated harassment policy reflecting 2020 Title IX changes, amended to ensure the inclusion of correct local contact information.

items.title: Superintendent’s Updates and Grant Announcement
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent shared updates on senior class events and announced a $350,000 Cummings Foundation grant awarded to the CCSR program over ten years.

items.title: COVID-19 Health and Masking Update
items.summary: The district announced that Medford is in the 'green zone' and that masks will be optional for K-8 students during outdoor recess beginning June 1st.

items.title: Introduction of Harvard Superintendent Resident
items.summary: The committee formally introduced Carmen Williams, a doctoral candidate from the Harvard Graduate School of Education, as the district's resident for the upcoming school year.

items.title: Acceptance of Church Donation
items.summary: Accepted a $10,000 donation from Impact Church for the McGlynn School to support specialized technology enhancements and school-based activities.

items.title: Elementary School Year-End Highlights
items.summary: Principals from the Brooks and Columbus schools presented overviews of school culture, academic projects, and social-emotional learning initiatives implemented during the pandemic.

items.title: FY22 Budget Update
items.summary: Administration provided an update on the $69.9 million budget request, outlining the use of ESSER funds to cover one-time instructional recovery costs.

items.title: Columbus School Renaming Extension
items.summary: Approved a deadline extension until June 7th for the advisory committee to submit its naming recommendation following community feedback regarding the process.

items.title: K-8 Student Email Whitelisting Resolution
items.summary: Referred a proposal to allow parents to email K-8 students directly to the Communications Subcommittee to address data management and network safety concerns.

items.title: Return to In-Person Public Meetings
items.summary: Voted to resume in-person meetings at City Hall starting June 7th, utilizing a hybrid model to preserve remote public participation capabilities.
